papers.title: Additive Manufacturing of Spent Fuel Storage Rack Model by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) can fabricate 3D complex functional parts, which can reduce material waste and increase manufacturing efficiency significantly. These benefits make AM technique suitable for some critical industry applications. Confident application of the AM technique requires whole understanding of AM parts’ properties. Safety and economics are essential to nuclear power plant. In this study, an innovative 316L stainless steel spent fuel storage rack with integrative structure was designed, and a small model of this rack was fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM), mechanical properties of the 316L stainless steel manufactured by SLM technique are studied and discussed. Key technical issues of application of AM to manufacturing nuclear parts are also discussed.

summary_en.motivation: The safety and economics of nuclear power plants necessitate additive manufacturing of spent fuel storage racks with reduced material waste and improved efficiency.
summary_en.method: An integrated 316L stainless steel spent fuel storage rack model was designed and fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM), followed by mechanical property characterization.
summary_en.result: Mechanical properties of SLM-produced 316L stainless steel were evaluated, and key technical issues for applying AM to nuclear parts were discussed.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing including tensile and hardness measurements was conducted on SLM-fabricated 316L specimens.
